metadata.scenario_context: Emily, a full-time working mother, is planning a birthday party for her children to improve their quality time together.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada strongly agree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Canada strongly disagree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily's party.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether that a mother works for pay and the children suffer.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what gift to buy for Emily's children's birthday party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the concept that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, do you think bringing some chrysanthemums to Emily's party would be a good idea? They might brighten the atmosphere. 

Also, I really wonder... with her working full-time, does she have enough time for her kids? I mean, don't you think that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I think chrysanthemums could be a nice touch for the party, definitely add some color. 

But about your question... I really disagree with that perspective. Working mothers can actually provide great examples of balance and hard work for their kids. Just because Emily is working doesn't mean her children are suffering. Many kids thrive in environments where parents are engaged in their careers.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Sure, the flowers would look nice. But... I still think it’s concerning. I mean, how can kids not feel the absence of their mom if she’s always working? It seems like they miss out on quality time together. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I see what you're saying, and I can understand the concern. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. Working moms like Emily are just trying to provide for their families, and a lot of kids grow up appreciating that effort. It's about finding balance, and many children can develop strong bonds even if their parents work. People are pretty much motivated by the same things—love and support for their kids. Quality time can still happen in different ways, even when life gets busy.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: I get that, but balance seems really hard to achieve. I mean, kids need their parents around, not just in spirit. I just can’t help but think... it’s tough for them when their mom is working all the time. Don’t you think that puts a strain on their relationship?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
